plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with tiny, fragrant violet-blue flowers. Fields of it hum with bees and scent the warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, peaking from late June through July
plants.location: Provence, France, and similar Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall stems carry broad golden-petaled blooms with dark seed-filled centers. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, so whole fields seem to face the same way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn, with early plantings opening around late June and July
plants.location: Temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere, including the central United States and southern Europe
plants.funFact: What looks like one flower is actually hundreds of tiny florets packed into a head. The florets are arranged in spirals that follow the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A huge, bowl-shaped bloom with a crown of pink, silky-tipped bracts around a downy center. It is South Africa's national flower and one of the most dramatic flowers in the world.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak flowering from late winter to spring (August to November), with scattered blooms in the cooler months from autumn on
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants and evolved to survive fire. Their thick underground stems resprout after wildfires sweep through the fynbos.
